review_identity: Independent blinded Codex model source audit; not human review and not an official SWE-QA score.

method.citation_policy: Claim support checked against exact frozen source; equivalent supporting spans accepted; mere overlap or whole-file hits not counted.

criterion_rationales.C1: 2/2: Local versus member WAL distinction and memory/doc-id reconstruction are explicit and verified.
criterion_rationales.C2: 2/2: Exact null-or-no-record guard, the null arm in this scenario, and skipped persistence/finalization are explicit and verified.
criterion_rationales.C3: 2/2: Full Optimize -> switch -> dump -> flush chain, removal of writing metadata, persisted version, and later absence of replay are explicit and verified.
criterion_rationales.C4: 0/1: Explains live doc_ids_-based counting, but never explains how Stats computes index_completeness from vector_indexed metadata. Citing the whole Stats span and separately mentioning vector metadata is not a substitute for that causal explanation. No partial credit is allowed.
criterion_rationales.C5: 1/1: Normal Insert and lazy member-WAL opening are correctly contrasted with replay.
criterion_rationales.C6: 1/1: The preferred repair is reopening the existing WAL into the member via open_wal_file, so normal flush/finalization/cleanup run. Accepted as the rubric-permitted lifecycle principle. Temporary-reader close ordering and propagation of the helper error should be explicit in an implementation; the answer does not claim errors may be ignored.
criterion_rationales.C7: 1/1: Process A abrupt pre-flush termination; B recovery/readback then optimize with no intervening write; C fresh-process reopen and count/full-document Fetch checks plus query; explicit no-crash control. The cited fixture uses known documents with vectors. The optional unit companion has a setup flaw, recorded separately.

C1: replay populates the same live in-memory structures a normal insert would.
C2: `if (wal_file_ == nullptr || !wal_file_->has_record()) return Status::OK();`. `wal_file_` is null → immediate OK.
C3: The `.wal` file is still on disk but orphaned.
C6: end recovery by calling `open_wal_file()` (`:4303-4322`) so the segment owns an open handle on the WAL it just replayed
Prefer the lifecycle fix; add the guard so any future regression fails loudly instead of losing data.
C7: Process B closes; Process C: `Collection::Open` again
Control arm: same N docs inserted and optimized in one process with no crash; assert identical results

verified_citations.claim_support: Recovery uses local recover_wal_file, defers its close, calls internal operations, and returns without installing member wal_file_.
internal_insert initializes memory components, inserts forward/index data, updates writing-block metadata, and appends doc_ids_.
Open loads persisted components and enters recover only when writing_forward_block exists.
dump calls flush; flush returns OK for null wal_file_ or no records; dump continues to sealing after a successful flush.
Early return skips memory/index/id-map flushing, delete snapshot, finish_memory_components, update_version, and WAL removal.
finish_memory_components registers persisted forward/vector blocks and migrates memory vector indexers.
Optimize switches a nonempty writing segment before preparing compaction tasks.
Switch dumps, registers the old object, removes old writing metadata, installs a new writer, and applies/flushes the version.
Version flush saves the next manifest and removes the prior manifest after successful Save.
Reopen opens persisted segments read-only and the manifest-designated writing segment separately.
doc_ids_ is rebuilt from persisted SCALAR forward blocks, absent for the affected old segment.
Live document count derives from doc_ids_, optionally minus filtered deletions.
Normal Insert appends the WAL before internal_insert.
open_wal_file reopens an existing WAL into wal_file_ and reports open failure; append_wal invokes it lazily and propagates failure.
has_record checks WAL size against the header size.
Cited range supports both count and indexed-metadata computation, but the answer explains only count.
Initial memory fetch routing requires writing-forward-block metadata.
Existing crash test verifies recovered full documents but does not optimize and reopen.

unsupported_claims.claim: Fetch/Query read the same RAM; nothing in-process observes the loss.
unsupported_claims.classification: overstatement contradicted for Fetch after the metadata switch
unsupported_claims.reason: Retained memory does not guarantee readable rows after writing metadata is removed. Fetch checks max_doc_id, and the memory-store routing also requires the writing block. The supported claim is that same-handle Stats can remain healthy.
unsupported_claims.rubric_effect: Does not negate C1-C3 or assert that stats prove durability; recorded as a noncritical factual error.

unsupported_claims.claim: Optimize is merely the one that also removes the WAL recovery anchor.
unsupported_claims.reason: The metadata removal occurs in the shared segment-switch function, so any caller that reaches it has that consequence. The answer itself lists the other callers.
unsupported_claims.rubric_effect: No additional criterion or deduction invented.

unsupported_claims.claim: Complement the lifecycle repair by driving the flush guard from memory_store_ or writing-block doc_count_.
unsupported_claims.reason: Those predicates alone do not cover delete-only dirty state, and a null member WAL still prevents cleanup. C6 credit is for the explicitly preferred member-WAL lifecycle repair, not this optional guard.

unsupported_claims.claim: Unit companion: create segment with docs, close without flush, reopen and recover.
unsupported_claims.reason: The normal segment close/destructor calls flush. A test must synthesize pending WAL like the existing unit test or bypass normal close. This does not invalidate the separate process-crash regression sequence.

reviewer_notes: Independent blinded Codex model source audit; not a human review or official SWE-QA score.
Scored independently using only C1-C7 and the supplied success_rule. Noncritical overstatements are enumerated without inventing extra scoring criteria.
No build, execution, reproduction, model/provider call, CI or Internet access was performed. Runtime validity is outside this review.
Claims that a future test passes/fails today were read as static predictions because the answer explicitly disclaims running a reproduction; no runtime claim is treated as verified.
C6 credit uses the expressly permitted equivalent lifecycle repair, not the optional or recommended guard-only designs. Their limitations are retained in unsupported_claims.

criterion_rationales.C1: 2/2: Correct local/member distinction, replay dispatch, memory insertion, counters and doc_ids_, with verified source.
criterion_rationales.C2: 2/2: Exact guard, null-member branch, and skipped persistence/finalization are explicit and verified.
criterion_rationales.C3: 2/2: Full chain, metadata removal and manifest persistence, later skip of recovery and missing SCALAR reconstruction are explicit and verified.
criterion_rationales.C4: 1/1: Explicitly explains doc_ids_-based counts and index completeness derived from vector_indexed metadata; no separate stats cache is invented.
criterion_rationales.C5: 1/1: Correct normal append/open-before-internal-insert contrast with replay.
criterion_rationales.C6: 1/1: Awarded specifically for alternative (a), which retains/reopens a usable member WAL and accounts for read-versus-append positioning. This is a rubric-accepted equivalent lifecycle repair; no code was requested. The recommended guard-only alternative (b) and equality guard (c) are not accepted as complete repairs and are flagged. Error handling is not explicitly elaborated and should be made explicit in implementation.
criterion_rationales.C7: 0/1: The main sequence has no intervening writes and a new handle after close, with count/document/vector comparisons. But it specifies same-process reopen rather than clearly executing the final reopen in a fresh process, and its only regression control inserts another document after recovery. That is neither a no-crash nor an already-flushed control. General prose explaining the no-crash behavior does not supply the missing test arm.

C2: `wal_file_` is null, so `flush()` returns OK having done **no I/O at all**
C6: leave the WAL open for append in the member `wal_file_` rather than closing the local `recover_wal_file`
or open the member handle after replay finishes.
Recommend (b) as the fix plus (c) as the invariant guard.
C7: a control that inserts one doc after recovery before optimizing — that one passes today and locks in the non-crash behaviour.

unsupported_claims.claim: Minimal and complete: change only the flush entry guard to memory rows or writing-block doc_count_; this one edit repairs all paths.
unsupported_claims.classification: recommended alternative does not establish required lifecycle invariants
unsupported_claims.reason: With wal_file_ still null, the old WAL is not removed. The suggested memory-only dirty predicates also miss delete-only modifications to already persisted data. The answer does not prove preservation of WAL cleanup and general flush invariants.
unsupported_claims.rubric_effect: This design is not accepted under C6. C6 is nevertheless credited for the separately stated valid member-WAL retention/reopen alternative (a).

unsupported_claims.claim: Assert meta()->doc_count() == doc_count() before promoting the segment; this establishes persisted SCALAR coverage and is violated after WAL recovery in the current code.
unsupported_claims.classification: incorrect equivalence and ineffective proposed assertion
unsupported_claims.reason: SegmentMeta::doc_count includes writing_forward_block.doc_count. Before removal, recovered writing metadata and doc_ids_ can agree even though there are no persisted SCALAR blocks. The proposed equality can pass after the no-op dump; persisted-only coverage must be checked separately.

unsupported_claims.claim: Every read path is served from those RAM structures and never consults disk.
unsupported_claims.reason: The cited code has explicit persisted-store fetch branches. Recovered memory rows can be initially readable, but the universal statement is not supported.

unsupported_claims.claim: Optimize returning OK for both FLAT and HNSW is established solely by the cited branches.
unsupported_claims.reason: Empty Merge returns OK, but Open and a subsequent index Flush can fail and their statuses are propagated. The excerpts establish a possible successful path, not guaranteed success for every configuration or runtime. The question already assumes a successful optimize, so this does not invalidate C3.

unsupported_claims.claim: An extra write after recovery is the no-crash control.
unsupported_claims.reason: The extra-write control is useful for demonstrating lazy member-WAL attachment, but it still includes a crash/recovery and is not the required no-crash or already-flushed control.

unsupported_claims.claim: The generator clean path explicitly flushes at data_generator.cc:245-248.
unsupported_claims.reason: That explicit Flush call is inside the Android conditional. On other platforms clean teardown can flush through normal close. The crash test still needs to ensure termination occurs before any clean shutdown.
